rationale_evidence.anchor: The Step series and its mature self-attack habit
rationale_evidence.statement: The final regime of the discovery corpus (2026-08-27 to 08-28) is the Step series: one hundred fifty-eight numbered steps that built the formal model Part III describes, and, in the same breath, the corpus's habit of attacking its own newest work reached its mature form.

Step 121 found the self-governing-policy gap first on the formal side: the machinery of admission was governed by a policy that nothing versioned and no one owned ('critical governance gap', the record says). The era's own freeze decisions -- stopping parts of the model mid-flight with no governing act -- were the same disease in behavioral form. The falsification pass would later catch the synthesized model repeating it, and the conformance pass would find its mildest cousin on the repository side. Four sightings; III.8 tells what the ratified architecture did about it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: What the era did not do: non-decisions and the late-and-narrow finding
rationale_evidence.statement: The era never selected an aggregation operator; never resolved the Lord name; never adopted or rejected Atma-Kernel; never wrote down the no-skip rule it mostly practiced; and -- the archaeology's sharpest structural finding -- it produced its central concepts late and narrow: the EpistemicContract enters at Steps 023/024; the AcceptancePolicy appears in exactly four documents. The concepts Part III leans on hardest are among the corpus's youngest. Their weight is formal depth and the testing they attracted, not breadth of occurrence -- a fact the reader deserves to weigh, and the final rule requires the book to hand over.
